rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) AS Year, g.Name AS Genre,
         SUM(il.UnitPrice * il.Quantity) AS Revenue
  FROM InvoiceLine il
  JOIN Invoice i ON il.InvoiceId = i.InvoiceId
  JOIN Track t ON il.TrackId = t.TrackId
  JOIN Genre g ON t.GenreId = g.GenreId
  GROUP BY Year, Genre
),
r AS (
  SELECT Year, Genre, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY Year ORDER BY Revenue DESC) AS rk
  FROM rev
)
SELECT Year, Genre FROM r WHERE rk = 2 ORDER BY Year;
rows.note: I'm taking revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity from InvoiceLine, grouped by the invoice's calendar year and the track's genre, with ties at second place all shown.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS customers_spent_more_2013
FROM (
  SELECT c.CustomerId,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2013' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2013,
         COALESCE(SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', i.InvoiceDate) = '2012' THEN i.Total END), 0) AS total_2012
  FROM Customer c
  LEFT JOIN Invoice i ON i.CustomerId = c.CustomerId
  GROUP BY c.CustomerId
) t
WHERE total_2013 > total_2012;
rows.note: I'll compare each customer's invoice totals for 2013 and 2012, counting customers whose 2013 total is higher than their 2012 total (customers with no invoices in a year count as 0).

rows.sql: SELECT AVG(Total) AS median_total FROM (SELECT Total FROM Invoice ORDER BY Total LIMIT 2 - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) % 2 OFFSET ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice) - 1) / 2)

WITH counts AS (
  SELECT ar.ArtistId, ar.Name, COUNT(DISTINCT pt.PlaylistId) AS PlaylistCount
  FROM Artist ar
  JOIN Album al ON al.ArtistId = ar.ArtistId
  JOIN Track t ON t.AlbumId = al.AlbumId
  JOIN PlaylistTrack pt ON pt.TrackId = t.TrackId
  GROUP BY ar.ArtistId, ar.Name
)
SELECT Name, PlaylistCount
FROM counts
WHERE PlaylistCount = (SELECT MAX(PlaylistCount) FROM counts);
rows.note: Assumption: count distinct playlists per artist via Track → Album → Artist, and return only the top artist(s), with ties included.

rows.sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Invoice), 2) AS avg_line_items_per_invoice FROM InvoiceLine
rows.note: Assuming "line items" means rows in InvoiceLine, and the average is taken over all invoices (including any with zero lines).

rows.sql:
WITH yearly AS (
  SELECT od.ProductID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2021' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2021,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2022' THEN od.Quantity ELSE 0 END) AS units_2022
  FROM "Order Details" od
  JOIN Orders o ON o.OrderID = od.OrderID
  GROUP BY od.ProductID
),
diffs AS (
  SELECT y.ProductID, p.ProductName, y.units_2021, y.units_2022,
         y.units_2022 - y.units_2021 AS increase
  FROM yearly y
  JOIN Products p ON p.ProductID = y.ProductID
)
SELECT ProductID, ProductName, units_2021, units_2022, increase
FROM diffs
WHERE increase = (SELECT MAX(increase) FROM diffs);
rows.note: I'm assuming "units sold" means the sum of `Quantity` in Order Details, grouped by the year of `OrderDate`.

rows.sql:
SELECT s.CompanyName AS ShipperName,
       ROUND(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN o.ShippedDate > o.RequiredDate THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / COUNT(*), 1) AS LatePercentage
FROM Orders o
JOIN Shippers s ON s.ShipperID = o.ShipVia
WHERE o.ShippedDate IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY s.ShipperID, s.CompanyName
ORDER BY s.CompanyName;
rows.note: Assumption: "shipped orders" means orders with a non-NULL ShippedDate, and "arrived after the required date" means ShippedDate > RequiredDate.

rows.sql: SELECT yr AS Year, cnt AS OrdersInYear, SUM(cnt) OVER (ORDER BY yr ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW) AS CumulativeOrders FROM (SELECT CAST(strftime('%Y', OrderDate) AS INTEGER) AS yr, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM Orders GROUP BY yr) ORDER BY yr
rows.note: Assuming "orders by year" means counting rows in Orders grouped by the year of OrderDate, with a cumulative count in year order.

rows.sql:
SELECT COUNT(*) AS orders_over_10000
FROM (
  SELECT OrderID, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity * (1 - Discount)) AS total
  FROM "Order Details"
  GROUP BY OrderID
  HAVING total > 10000
) t;
rows.note: Assumption: total value per order = sum of UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) over its "Order Details" lines, and orders with no line items are excluded.

rows.sql:
WITH rev AS (
  SELECT o.EmployeeID,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2018' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2018,
         SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y', o.OrderDate) = '2019' THEN od.UnitPrice * od.Quantity * (1 - od.Discount) ELSE 0 END) AS rev2019
  FROM Orders o
  JOIN "Order Details" od ON od.OrderID = o.OrderID
  GROUP BY o.EmployeeID
),
diff AS (
  SELECT r.EmployeeID, r.rev2018, r.rev2019, (r.rev2019 - r.rev2018) AS growth
  FROM rev r
)
SELECT e.FirstName || ' ' || e.LastName AS FullName, d.rev2018, d.rev2019, d.growth
FROM diff d
JOIN Employees e ON e.EmployeeID = d.EmployeeID
WHERE d.growth = (SELECT MAX(growth) FROM diff)
rows.note: I'll sum line revenue as UnitPrice × Quantity × (1 − Discount) by order year, take the 2019 minus 2018 change per employee, and return the employee(s) with the largest increase.
